clean_story:
Interchangeable parts. Systems built like blocks.

The term modular design comes from the Latin modulus, meaning a small measure, as each part is a self-contained unit of function. A bicycle wheel can be swapped without rebuilding the frame. A smartphone case snaps on and off, leaving the phone intact. This works because each module has a clear job and a standard way to connect—like train cars coupling with identical hooks. Factories use it to assemble cars faster. Software uses it to update apps without breaking the whole program. Lego bricks are modular: one piece fits countless others, yet each stays distinct. The Burj Khalifa used modular construction, lifting pre-built sections to the sky like stacking giant steel boxes. Three related subjects are prefabrication, plug and play hardware and adaptive systems.
